objective: Follow-up to DISTANCE-INFO-20261117-001 and the owner's answer on A97 (distance has no direction and gives an order in which nothing is skipped): prove or refute that how often two distinctions differ (the differ count) determines every not-all-equal base, and test whether the candidate distances (differ count, bond distance, steps apart) are built from unit steps and give an order from any starting distinction. Serves G1 and G16; tests A97.
status: Complete 2026-11-17 (Successful; referee pending): where knots form no cycle, one distance read from the allowed states does both jobs (tau = -log_3|1 - 2d/N| equals steps apart, proved); with cycles of knots they split: the disagreement count determines every not-all-equal base from four distinctions (proved; fails at three, one knot against none) but on the thread, knot chain and weave nothing lies between anything (computed, 9 of 9 frozen predictions held), while steps apart and bond distance have the order without all the information. Order lives in knots: betweenness is a three-place constraint, and a chain of m distinctions allows at most 2m joint values. A97 narrowed, under challenge; A98 new.
stop_rule: One proof and one frozen computation with its read-out; A97 status set; referee hand-off; report.
title: Which distance carries a base's information, and which gives an order with nothing skipped
